guide.summary: Roman remains, Georgian museums and a thermal spa, with markets, bakeries, dinners and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Several museums keep to a Tuesday-to-Sunday pattern: the Herschel Museum of Astronomy is closed on Mondays outside local school and bank holidays, and the American Museum & Gardens also opens Tuesday to Sunday until 3 January 2027.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Sotto Sotto is closed on Mondays and Sundays, Sub 13 on Sundays and Mondays, and Corkage on Sundays. The Herschel Museum of Astronomy closes on Mondays except during local school holidays and bank holidays.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Roman Baths tickets are sold only through romanbaths.co.uk, and guided tours should be pre-booked. At the Herschel Museum of Astronomy you can pay on the door, but booking online is recommended.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Sally Lunn's takes no daytime reservations except for its set afternoon tea at 15.30; book for evening dinner. The Dark Horse accepts walk-ins when possible but says it is frequently fully booked.

toolkit.label: Age and dress
toolkit.copy: Thermae Bath Spa admits guests aged 16 and over, 18 for treatments, with proof of age required. The Dark Horse is 21s and over and does not allow fancy dress, including hen party attire.

guide.dek: Book the Roman Baths and Thermae Bath Spa online, then plan museum days around Monday closures.
intro: Bath packs its headline sights into a few walkable streets. The Roman Baths on Abbey Church Yard sell tickets only through their own website, and you should pre-book any guided tour. Next door, Bath Abbey opens from 10am Monday to Saturday and from 1pm to 3:30pm on Sunday, with last entry 30 minutes before closing. For a soak in the hot springs, Thermae Bath Spa on Hot Bath Street opens 09:00 to 21:30, with pools closing at 21:00; you must be 16 or over, and 18 for treatments.

For a gallery day, the Holburne Museum on Great Pulteney Street opens Monday to Saturday from 10am and Sunday from 11am, and its Eric Ravilious exhibition on the artists of the chalk downs runs from 3 October 2026 to 10 January 2027. The Herschel Museum of Astronomy on New King Street shows Photology, on John Herschel, Henry Talbot and early photography, until 3 January 2027; under-18s go free with an adult. On Gay Street, the Jane Austen Centre opens daily 10am to 5:30pm and has its Regency Tea Room.

Further out, Beckford's Tower on Lansdown Road opens on Saturdays and Sundays from 31 October to 13 December 2026, 10am to 4pm. The American Museum & Gardens at Claverton Manor opens Tuesday to Sunday until 3 January 2027, and its car park is free for visitors. For food shopping, the Guildhall Market on High Street opens Monday to Saturday, 8am to 5pm, and Green Park Station hosts Bath Farmers' Market every weekend. Sally Lunn's on North Parade Passage opens every day from 10:00, and Landrace on Walcot Street runs a bakery shop and cafe from 8:30am on weekdays.

In the evening, book ahead where you can. Sotto Sotto on North Parade calls itself very small and strongly recommends booking. Corkage on Chapel Row serves Christmas menus from 24 November to 23 December 2026. At The Olive Tree, in The Queensberry Hotel, a change or cancellation needs 48 hours' notice. For a drink, The Dark Horse on Kingsmead Square admits only over-21s and recommends a reservation, while Sub 13 on Edgar Buildings opens until 3am on Fridays and Saturdays.
summaryCards: Pair the Roman Baths, booked online, with Bath Abbey next door, then end the day at Thermae Bath Spa.
Start with brunch at The Pump Room or a loaf from Landrace, then browse the Guildhall Market before the Holburne Museum opens.
Check closing days: Sotto Sotto and Sub 13 shut on Mondays and Sundays, and the Herschel Museum of Astronomy is closed most Mondays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The National Trust's Bath Assembly Rooms and Prior Park pages showed a bot check, Victoria Art Gallery's visit and contact pages refused automated reading (so its address could not be confirmed), and Colonna Coffee, Picnic Coffee, Comins Tea House, The Raven and GAIL's returned rate-limit errors; none of these failures is evidence of closure. Several confirmed places publish hours only partially or not at all (No.1 Royal Crescent, The Circus Restaurant, The Royal Crescent Hotel & Spa, The Gainsborough Bath Spa, The Bath Priory, Clayton's Kitchen, Green Park Station), Landrace and Noya's Kitchen show conflicting restaurant hours, and Bath Abbey's address is its published postal address. No standalone coffee shop could be confirmed, so the coffee list uses cafés and tea rooms.
